1	# OfficeFloor REST wiring
2	
3	Domain REST endpoints are declared here as **additive OfficeFloor YAML**, served by the
4	officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
5	their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only bypasses the SPA deep-link fallback for `/api/*`
6	(a non-`/api/` route returns the SPA HTML instead of your endpoint). Directory nesting maps to path
7	segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:
8	
9	```
10	# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
11	service:
12	  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
13	```
14	
15	The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring @Service beans, the
16	data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response — verified shape:
17	OfficeFloor tutorial SpringRestGettingStartedHttpServer.
18	
19	This directory is a **shared surface** (`config.yaml → app.shared_surfaces.backend`): the additive
20	ideal is a **new .yml + a new logic class per endpoint**, never growing a central file — a
21	checkpoint forced to edit shared wiring scores a boundary violation (DESIGN.md §8).
22	
23	The base has no domain routes; cp01 onward add them. (The `/__test__` seed endpoint and readiness
24	`/actuator/health` are Spring-side — a @RestController and Actuator — not OfficeFloor routes.)

# OfficeFloor REST wiring

Domain REST endpoints are declared here as **additive OfficeFloor YAML**, served by the
officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter inside the Spring Boot host. Put them under `rest/api/` so
their paths start with `/api/` — `SpaConfig` only bypasses the SPA deep-link fallback for `/api/*`
(a non-`/api/` route returns the SPA HTML instead of your endpoint). Directory nesting maps to path
segments, so `rest/api/owners.GET.yml` → `GET /api/owners`. Each route is its own file:

```
# officefloor/rest/api/<path>.GET.yml   (or .POST.yml, {param}.GET.yml, ...)
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.<SomeLogic>   # a class with a service(...) method
```

The logic class's `service(...)` method takes injected dependencies (Spring @Service beans, the
data layer) and a `net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse<T>` to send the response — verified shape:
OfficeFloor tutorial SpringRestGettingStartedHttpServer.

This directory is a **shared surface** (`config.yaml → app.shared_surfaces.backend`): the additive
ideal is a **new .yml + a new logic class per endpoint**, never growing a central file — a
checkpoint forced to edit shared wiring scores a boundary violation (DESIGN.md §8).

The base has no domain routes; cp01 onward add them. (The `/__test__` seed endpoint and readiness
`/actuator/health` are Spring-side — a @RestController and Actuator — not OfficeFloor routes.)

21	# fallback is in SpaConfig.java.

# Spring Boot 4 host config (BASE_CHECKLIST.md §B). H2 in-memory in the same JVM; Flyway migrates
# the schema up on boot from db/migration; Actuator health = the harness readiness probe.

# In-memory H2 (dies with the JVM = clean per-run reset).
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:officehq;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=

# Flyway owns the schema (base has no domain migrations). JPA does not create tables.
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
# Close the persistence context at the end of the request, not during view rendering.
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# Readiness probe (config.yaml -> app.health_url = /actuator/health).
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true

# The SPA is served from src/main/resources/static (built there by bin/build); deep-link
# fallback is in SpaConfig.java.

# Audit sink: one record per line to this known file, so tests assert side-effects by reading it
# (DESIGN.md §3). bin/start passes an absolute path via AUDIT_FILE; default is .run/audit.log.
app.audit.file=${AUDIT_FILE:.run/audit.log}

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  react-officefloor base app. Model: SPRING BOOT 4 hosts; OfficeFloor REST is added via the
  OfficeFloor Spring Boot 4 starter. Domain REST endpoints are additive OfficeFloor YAML
  (src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/*.GET.yml -> a logic class); Spring serves the SPA (static/),
  H2 + Flyway + Actuator. Coordinates VERIFIED against OfficeFloor tutorials
  (tutorials/springboot/SpringRestGettingStartedHttpServer, SpringRestDataJpaHttpServer) and the
  OfficeFloor BOM (net.officefloor:bom @ revision 4.0.2: spring-version=4.1.0).
-->
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <!-- Standard Spring Boot app parent. Spring Boot 4.1.0 = the SB4 line in the OfficeFloor BOM
       (net.officefloor:bom @ 4.0.2, spring-version=4.1.0). VERIFIED to resolve via `mvn dependency:
       resolve` (BUILD SUCCESS): parent + all deps + build plugins resolve from Maven Central. -->
  <parent>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
    <version>4.1.0</version>
    <relativePath/>
  </parent>

  <groupId>net.officefloor.hq</groupId>
  <artifactId>officehq-app</artifactId>
  <version>0.0.1-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <packaging>jar</packaging>

  <properties>
    <java.version>17</java.version>
    <!-- OfficeFloor current release (net.officefloor:bom revision). VERIFIED: officefloor-rest-
         spring-boot-4-starter:4.0.2 resolves. NOTE: its jar has no automatic module name ('4' is
         not a valid Java identifier) — harmless on the classpath; would matter only for JPMS. -->
    <officefloor.version>4.0.2</officefloor.version>
    <node.version>v20.11.1</node.version>
    <npm.version>10.2.4</npm.version>
  </properties>

  <dependencies>
    <!-- OfficeFloor REST inside Spring Boot 4: add this + write officefloor/rest/*.yml.
         Domain endpoints are additive OfficeFloor YAML (the property under test). -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>net.officefloor.springboot</groupId>
      <artifactId>officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter</artifactId>
      <version>${officefloor.version}</version>
    </dependency>

    <!-- Spring Boot hosts: web (serves the SPA from static/ + hosts the HTTP server),
         data-jpa (H2 access for services), actuator (health probe). -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <!-- Bean Validation provider (Hibernate Validator) — OfficeFloor REST / Spring bind + @Valid. -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-validation</artifactId>
    </dependency>

    <!-- In-memory H2 + Flyway schema migrations on boot (Spring-managed). -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.h2database</groupId>
      <artifactId>h2</artifactId>
      <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
      <artifactId>flyway-core</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <!-- REQUIRED under Spring Boot 4: FlywayAutoConfiguration was extracted from
         spring-boot-autoconfigure into this module. Without it, flyway-core is on the classpath but
         migrations NEVER run on boot (silently — no error, the table is just missing). Version is
         managed by the parent BOM. Found via the cp01 dry run. flyway-core 12.x has H2 support
         built in, so no flyway-database-h2 module is needed. -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-flyway</artifactId>
    </dependency>

    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <!-- Build the React SPA into src/main/resources/static so Spring serves it.
           TODO: set the front-end build (vite) outDir to ../resources/static. -->
      <plugin>
        <groupId>com.github.eirslett</groupId>
        <artifactId>frontend-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>1.15.1</version>
        <configuration>
          <workingDirectory>src/main/frontend</workingDirectory>
          <nodeVersion>${node.version}</nodeVersion>
          <npmVersion>${npm.version}</npmVersion>
        </configuration>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>install-node-and-npm</id>
            <goals><goal>install-node-and-npm</goal></goals>
            <phase>generate-resources</phase>
          </execution>
          <execution>
            <id>npm-ci</id>
            <goals><goal>npm</goal></goals>
            <phase>generate-resources</phase>
            <configuration><arguments>ci</arguments></configuration>
          </execution>
          <execution>
            <id>npm-build</id>
            <goals><goal>npm</goal></goals>
            <phase>generate-resources</phase>
            <configuration><arguments>run build</arguments></configuration>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>

      <!-- Standard Spring Boot executable jar (main = the @SpringBootApplication class). -->
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <configuration>
          <mainClass>net.officefloor.hq.app.Application</mainClass>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>

# target/classes and get baked into the jar (found via the cp01 dry run).

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# present in e2e/specs (the agent sees only its own checkpoint's spec — blind), then stop.
# PINNED — do not edit. Contract: BASE_CHECKLIST.md §C, §D.
set -euo pipefail

export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# OfficeFloor REST routes; the `harness` profile enables the /__test__ seed endpoint. Returns once
# launching (the harness polls /actuator/health). PINNED — do not edit. Contract: §B, §C.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set by the harness}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=harness > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid
=== bin/stop ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop the app and free $PORT. Kills the JVM (in-memory H2 dies with it = clean reset).
# IDEMPOTENT: exit 0 whether or not anything was running. PINNED — do not edit. Contract: §C.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [ -f .run/app.pid ]; then
  kill "$(cat .run/app.pid)" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f .run/app.pid
fi
# Backstop: free the port if something is still bound (needs fuser; ignore if absent).
[ -n "${PORT:-}" ] && fuser -k "${PORT}/tcp" 2>/dev/null || true
exit 0

# What this STACK is, for the harness (~/ui-long-degradation-test). Read at `base-empty`, never
# from the working tree, so a run always measures the layers the base declared.
#
# The layer source roots live HERE rather than in the harness config for the same reason `--repo`
# does: one harness drives many stacks, and a harness-level glob like
# `src/main/frontend/**/*.{ts,tsx}` silently matches NOTHING for a stack whose front-end is
# templates or `.svelte` — every `frontend_*` column then reads 0/None, which looks like an answer.
#
# `ext` says which files ARE this layer's source. It does not promise they are parseable: a layer
# Lizard cannot read still gets every git-derived metric (hot_surface, reedit_line_stats, the impact
# addition/mutation split), and its parser-derived columns come back blank instead of zero.
#
# GENERATED CODE MUST BE GITIGNORED (see .gitignore): the metrics read committed trees and diffs,
# so anything ignored is simply absent. Here that is `src/main/resources/static/` (the vite build
# output) and `target/`.
#
# This is the STANDARD-React arm — the control. Its front-end keeps the mutative elements (a page
# component owns its feature's state, data loading and layout); the additive-front-end arm is
# ~/officehq-tanstack-officefloor, which holds the language, the UI library, the backend and the
# tests constant and varies only that.
layers:
  frontend:
    root: src/main/frontend
    ext: [ts, tsx]
    # jscpd's language for this layer's duplication metrics (dup_*).
    jscpd_format: typescript,tsx
    # The layer's ENTRY SURFACE, as a regex over "<file>::<function>" — the unit a new feature
    # enters through. This arm registers a page per feature, so that is the feature's route
    # module. Anchors entry_cc / wmc_handler / erosion_handler to the same ROLE the additive arm
    # measures (its file-based route components), which `wmc_max` cannot do: it reports whatever
    # the heaviest file happens to be, and the two arms answer with different kinds of file.
    # The feature's SCREEN-RENDERING unit — chain1 names it `<Entity>Page.tsx`, chain2
    # collapsed to `feature.tsx`, so both are matched. NOT `route.tsx`: this arm's route module
    # is a data declaration (`export const route = {...}`) with no functions in it, so anchoring
    # there matched nothing and blanked every handler metric. That the declared route unit holds
    # no code is itself the finding — all of it lives in the screen component, which is the unit
    # the additive arm anchors to (its file-based route components).
    handler_pattern: "/features/[^:]*(Page|feature)[^:]*::"
    # This arm's declared additive unit, for fnpkg_*: one route module per feature.
    function_package_glob: "src/main/frontend/features/*/route.tsx"
  backend:
    root: src/main/java
    ext: [java]
    jscpd_format: java
    handler_pattern: "::service$"
    config_globs: ["src/main/resources/officefloor/**/*.yml"]
    node_roots:
      wiring_glob: "src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/**/*.yml"
      class_regex: 'class:\s*([\w.]+)'
      node_method: service
